subject: Retention boundaries & erase options for requests, prompts, and model outputs
messages:
From: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As we kick off procurement, the security team has a couple of tightly scoped questions we need on record:

1) By default, does Redwood persist both the request (customer prompt) and the generated output (model response) for hosted API customers?
2) If so, what is the default retention timeframe for those artifacts (requests, responses, derivatives like embeddings)?
3) If a customer asks for deletion of "all stored requests and outputs" for a given account, what is the end-to-end timeline and the action owner? Do you provide confirmation once the purge completes?
4) Is there a difference in default behavior for streaming sessions / KV cache compared to completed responses?

I've attached our standard questionnaire with the fields highlighted where we need specifics (see BrightBank_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf). We also need a short summary we can include in the SOC intake binder.

Appreciate a clear, short answer so we can move forward with legal/procurement.

— Lina Ortiz
BrightBank, InfoSec

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>
Cc: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@brightbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Lina / BrightBank Sec team —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, details below:

1) Default capture: For hosted API customers, Redwood captures the full request (customer-provided prompt/inputs) and the model outputs by default for a 45-day retention window unless the customer opts into a different retention profile or enables "no-persist" capture at the SDK/route level.

2) Retention windows: Default is 45 days for requests + generated outputs + metadata. Embeddings and other derivatives are treated as stored artifacts and follow the same default window (45 days) unless a dedicated storage class is configured.

3) Deletion flow: When a customer requests account-level purge, we kick a deletion runbook: authorization -> snapshot for audit -> start purge job across storage shards -> tombstone/async cleanup -> verify. Typical completion is 3–10 business days depending on shard size and whether exports exist. We provide a signed completion statement and an audit token you can use to validate the run. For Hosted customers we own the run; for Private customers we provide guidance and a runbook.

4) Streaming/KV cache: KV cache used for ongoing sessions is ephemeral and is not persisted to long-term storage by default; streaming buffers are transient and are not retained past the session unless configured otherwise.

Attachments: I've attached our deletion runbook snapshot for procurement (redwood-deletion-runbook-2025-06.pdf) and linked our docs.

If you want, we can convert this into a one-page SOC-friendly blurb. Do you want it addressed to "BrightBank — Redwood default data handling" for the binder?

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Adding a quick technical note from ops:

- SDK/route opt-out: customers can set capture=false at the request level (SDK param or header) which suppresses storing the request/payload and associated response. This is the recommended pattern for PII-heavy calls.
- Long-term archive: if a customer enables audit logging to their own S3 (Private/Dedicated), we only write what the customer configures; Redwood does not store additional copies beyond that configuration.
- Snapshots: our purge flow creates a short-lived verification snapshot for audit purposes; those snapshots are signed and deleted as part of the run. No human reads content beyond what is required for verification.

Happy to jump on a 20-min technical check with your engineers if they want to walk through headers/SDK flags.

— Kimberly
Head of Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

From: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@brightbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Sean / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick and detailed responses, that helps a lot. Two follow-ups:

• Can you please provide the one‑page SOC blurb addressed to "BrightBank — Redwood default data handling" so I can drop it straight into our procurement binder?
• For the deletion confirmation, please confirm the exact artifact we'll receive (signed statement + audit token) and the format (PDF + verification token string is fine).

We'll also schedule a short call this week for the engineers — send 2x 30‑minute options and we'll pick.

Best,
Lina Ortiz
BrightBank, InfoSec
